title: WHO: cause-of-death totals depend on registration, which is often incomplete
summary: The causes-of-death sheet says mortality data are still fragmented in many low-income countries, and it names ICD-11 as WHO's classification for causes.
body: WHO's causes-of-death fact sheet says that knowing why people die is how priorities are set, and that accurate mortality data remain a major challenge, particularly in many low-income countries. It says data systems are often fragmented, incomplete, or inconsistent, so policy-makers may lack reliable information on how many people die, when, and of what. It says WHO develops standards through the International Classification of Diseases, 11th revision, a digital platform for reporting causes of death. The death totals on the companion cards are estimates built on that uneven registration. They are not a complete count of every death.
